title: Restore Drill
user: Teams relying on managed Postgres backups who need to prove that a recent backup restores into their intended version and extension set before an outage.

evidence.quote_or_summary: An Ask HN report describes a production Supabase database remaining down for 37 hours after a billing downgrade and restoration steps.
A Supabase issue reports logical backup commands from PostgreSQL 17.6+ failing when restored to PostgreSQL 15.8.

recurrence: A recent outage report and a concrete backup-version incompatibility show that possessing an export does not prove a recoverable service.
current_workaround: Download a dump, assume it works, test restore only during an incident, or manually inspect SQL headers and extensions.
incumbents_and_gap: Managed providers create backups and pg_restore executes them; neither supplies a small recurring compatibility drill with a machine-readable receipt and known version/extension mismatch explanation.
smallest_useful_product: A local/container CLI that restores a selected sanitized or full backup into an explicit disposable Postgres version, checks extensions/roles/schema readiness, times the run, and writes a signed receipt. Non-goals: backup storage, production restore, or database hosting.
success_measure: A weekly pilot catches an intentionally introduced version or extension incompatibility before a recovery event and produces a pass/fail receipt in under 20 minutes.
monetization: one-time — a local recovery-control utility suits teams avoiding additional data-hosting vendors.
constraints: Use disposable isolated containers; encryption at rest for any saved dump; never run against production connection strings; account for provider backup terms and large-data cost.
why_distinct: It proves restore compatibility on a schedule rather than offering another backup destination or migration framework.
summary: Prove a Postgres backup restores before an outage
